courses.summary: This course provides a comprehensive deep dive in designing and implement Internet of Things (IoT) solutions on Microsoft Azure. The course covers both directions of message flow from device-to-cloud and cloud-to device, building analytics solutions atop the real-time telemetry, managing devices and securing the solution
objectives: This course provides a comprehensive deep dive in designing and implement Internet of Things (IoT) solutions on Microsoft Azure. The course covers both directions of message flow from device-to-cloud and cloud-to device, building analytics solutions atop the real-time telemetry, managing devices and securing the solution

In this introduction to Cloud Computing, we answer the key question “What is the cloud?” With a solid, standards based approach & examples from the real word, we look at all the definitions that come together to mean cloud.

In this module, we will explain how Microsoft Azure is a growing collection of integrated cloud services which developers and IT professionals use to build, deploy and manage applications through our global network of data centers
In this module, you learn how to use Azure Storage, a cloud storage service that is durable, available, and scalable.
This module includes Azure SQL Database which is a relational database-as-a service using the Microsoft SQL Server Engine.

This module includes Azure Cosmos DB which is a globally distributed database service designed to enable you to elastically & independently scale throughput & storage across any number of geographical regions with a comprehensive SLA. & how to use a series of popular APIs and programming models.

In this module, you will learn following azure services: How to use Hadoop in the cloud on HDInsight to analyze streaming or historical data. How data scientists & developers use Machine Learning to embed predictive analytics into applications. How to run internet of Things (IoT) analytics in the cloud with Stream Analytics, a fully managed event-processing engine. How to use Data Lake Analytics to run big data analysis jobs that scale to massive data sets. How to use Data Lake Store to create a hyper-scale, Hadoop-compatible repository for analytics on data of any size, type, and ingestion speed. How to use Data Factory, a cloud data integration service, to compose data storage, movement, and processing services into automated data pipelines. How to add data visualizations and interactive reports to applications with Power BI Embedded.

In this module, you will learn about Azure App Service which is a platform-as-a-service (PaaS) offering of Microsoft Azure. And explain how to Create web & mobile apps for any platform or device. Integrate your apps with SaaS solutions, connect with on-premises applications, and automate your business processes.
In this module, you will learn Azure Active Directory (Azure AD) Microsoft’s multi-tenant, cloud based directory and identity management service.

In today's cloud-enabled world, our enterprise customers' needs are multi-faceted evolving – balancing on- and off-premises workloads, securing their data wherever it lives and managing myriad business applications. In this module, we explain the vision to enable seamless integration among enterprise applications across cloud-native and hybrid deployments so our customers can achieve more.
Explore IoT smart sensor and actuator solution providers. Compare types and technical requirements and protocols across market industries.
In this module, we will explain current demand for IoT in various sectors & verticals. It will also explain with few use cases to understand IoT in depth.

In this module, we’ll start by discussing what IoT is, then we’ll discuss some basics around IoT Messaging as well as the Azure services available for building Internet of Things solutions in the cloud.

In this module, we’ll start by discussing the various IoT Devices and Platform available for building hardware Internet of Things devices. Then we’ll discuss the Azure Certified for IoT program & finally the different starter kits available for getting started building your hardware-based IoT devices.

In this module, we’ll discuss IoT Messaging Architecture in more detail. Then we’ll go into using the Azure IoT Hub to facilitate messaging with IoT Devices and send event data into the cloud. We’ll also discuss storage of event data by covering what the different storage options are in Azure. Finally, we’ll wrap up the module by going over Azure Event Hubs, and why you might use IoT Hub or Event Hubs for your messaging solutions.

In this module, we’ll discuss implementing Real-Time processing in an IoT solution. We’ll start by discussing stream processing using HDInsight & Azure Stream Analytics. processing data paths. Then we’ll talk about the purpose of Batch Processing & how it fits with a Lambda Architecture. We’ll also cover the features of both Azure Web Apps and Azure Functions for implementing background processing as part of real-time analytics and batch

In this module, we’ll discuss more detail surrounding Cloud-to-Device messaging & sending Command & Control messages to IoT Devices. We’ll discuss the features of Azure IoT Hub for Device Management such as the Device Lifecycle, the Device Registry, and Device Twins.

In this module, we’ll discuss what Machine Learning is & what Azure Machine Learning must offer. We’ll get into some of the specifics of how to use Azure Machine Learning to add intelligence & gain insights into your data. We’ll also discuss what Cortana Intelligence Suite offers.

In this module, we’ll discuss managing IoT devices & device provisioning with Azure IoT Hub. We’ll also discuss a couple IoT security vulnerabilities from recent past & why IoT Security is very important. We’ll discuss IoT Security best practices by dividing an IoT Architecture into several security zones, as well as other tips from both the hardware and software side of security.

In this module, you will use a Simulated IoT device (no hardware required) & services within Microsoft Azure to build an IoT solution that demonstrates bi-directional message flow (cloud-to-device and device-to-cloud) as well as message ingestion & analytics processing using Microsoft Azure IoT related services.

App development is at its peak now and so is the demand for apps that look, perform, and function as native apps. Creating apps that have a native performance capability requires having to write multiple code bases for each native platform; an exercise that results in an increased budget and extra effort.
